picks.intervention_label: IMA203 (PRAME-TCR-T) via ACTengine basket NCT03686124
picks.rationale: This is the biggest number in the dossier for a trial an osteosarcoma patient can actually enter: ORR 54% (95% CI 34-73) in the phase-1 basket, mDoR not reached, and the sarcoma cohort is named on the protocol rather than inferred. The patient's PRAME-RNA signal plus the Iura data (56% osteosarcoma PRAME IHC-positive, n=82) makes it a coin-flip that both gates confirm, and if they do this is a one-and-done cell infusion with the best response rate on the table. I want this one worked up first. The upside is a deep, durable remission from a single manufactured product.
primary_concerns: The 54% ORR comes from n=28 across mixed histologies, not osteosarcoma specifically, so the point estimate could shrink a lot in bone
Hard gate: needs both PRAME IHC-positive AND HLA-A*02:01-positive, and A*02:01 is only ~40-50% prevalent, so roughly half of patients are foreclosed before the tumor is even tested
Cy/Flu lymphodepletion plus ~100% CRS and one treatment-related septic death in the reported cohort; this is real toxicity, not a soft option

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab (DLL3 x CD3 BiTE) via basket NCT06788938
picks.rationale: The mechanism is proven where it has been tested: phase-3 OS HR 0.6 (95% CI 0.47-0.77) in SCLC, and the basket NCT06788938 explicitly opens the door to non-SCLC tumors that clear the DLL3 IHC gate. If the patient's DLL3 RNA translates to membrane protein at >=1% (>=25% gets stage-1 entry), an off-the-shelf drug with a phase-3 survival signal and a manageable CRS profile is available now, no manufacturing wait. The honest gap is that every efficacy row is SCLC and there is zero osteosarcoma clinical data. I take that bet because the ceiling and the drug's availability are both high.
primary_concerns: DLL3 in osteosarcoma may be intracellular or below the density BiTE killing needs; RNA does not prove membrane localization and the preclinical osteosarcoma data (Wang) never measured surface protein
IHC gate could return negative and close the whole DLL3 branch at once
CRS ~50% and ICANS-like events ~10% require inpatient step-up dosing; deliverable but not trivial

picks.intervention_label: brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC)
picks.rationale: Same PRAME target as my rank-1 but a lighter delivery: an off-the-shelf infusion with no lymphodepletion, and the PRAME-positive subset is where the signal lives (mPFS 4.5 vs 2.1 mo, 6-month OS 94% vs 40%). ORR is only 11% overall, so I am not pretending this is IMA203 on efficacy, but the safety-for-access trade is attractive and the NCI is running a dedicated sarcoma phase 2 (NCT07686367) that establishes the mechanism belongs in bone tumors. The catch: the pan-tumor basket sarcoma slot is active-not-recruiting, so this may hinge on the IMC-P115C successor or medical-affairs access rather than an open door today.
primary_concerns: 11% ORR is a thin single-agent number; the durable benefit is concentrated in a responder subset that may or may not include osteosarcoma
The osteosarcoma-relevant enrollment path is not open (NCI sarcoma trial names synovial and myxoid lipo, not bone; the basket sarcoma cohort is closed)
Requires the same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 double gate as IMA203, so it shares that eligibility bottleneck

picks.intervention_label: IMC-P115C (next-gen PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT07156136
picks.rationale: This is the open-door version of my rank-3: a recruiting pan-tumor PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 basket where non-melanoma histologies are accepted in principle, so if brenetafusp's slot stays shut this is the ImmTAC that a patient could actually enroll into today. As a next-generation successor it is engineered off brenetafusp's data, which is the reason I rank the mechanism at all. Pure phase-1 first-in-human, no efficacy readout yet, so I am buying the target and the platform, not a number.
primary_concerns: No human efficacy or safety data specific to IMC-P115C exists yet; this is a bet on the ImmTAC class and the PRAME target only
Sarcoma is not confirmed on the per-protocol list; needs medical-affairs verification before it is real
Same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 gate; both must confirm

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab + radiation therapy via NCT06814496
picks.rationale: If the DLL3 IHC confirms, this stacks an abscopal radiation rationale on top of the tarlatamab mechanism I already back at rank 2, and the pan-tumor DLL3-IHC gate could admit a positive osteosarcoma. The draw for a metastatic patient with irradiable sites is the chance that local RT primes a systemic response the BiTE then amplifies. I rank it below monotherapy tarlatamab because there is no combination efficacy or safety data at all, registry-only, so the incremental benefit over rank 2 is a hypothesis rather than a finding.
primary_concerns: Zero combination data: the abscopal benefit is a hypothesis and the added RT toxicity is exactly what this phase-1 is still characterizing
Same DLL3 IHC gate as rank 2, plus needs bone sarcoma confirmed on the per-protocol list and an extracranial site amenable to radiation
If DLL3 protein is absent, both this and rank 2 fall together

notes: Ranking is driven by expected effect size gated on the confirmatory tests, per efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.85 and the stated 'accepts high-risk high-reward' constraint. Rank order among the PRAME arms is deliberately efficacy-first (IMA203 54% ORR) then access-first (IMC-P115C is recruiting where brenetafusp's sarcoma slot is closed). Everything here is honestly gated: PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 for ranks 1/3/4, DLL3 SP347 IHC for ranks 2/5. I deliberately did not rank the SCLC-only DLL3 ADC/radioligand/CAR-T pipeline (ZL-1310, 225Ac agents, LB2102, etc.) because none is enrollable for a bone-sarcoma patient and none carries osteosarcoma-axis data that beats the four basket-eligible picks above. No abstain: the antigen axis matches the patient's exact biomarkers and at least two trials (NCT03686124, NCT06788938) are open baskets that admit the histology in principle. Note for the board: rank-5 cites PMID 36689692 (tarlatamab phase-1 SCLC safety) from the ce-3 evidence row's notes field as the safety anchor for the RT combination.

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab (DLL3 x CD3 BiTE) via DLL3-IHC-gated basket NCT06788938
picks.rationale: Of everything on the table this is the one agent with a real safety follow-up: DeLLphi-304 randomized 509 patients, G3+ treatment-related AEs ran 24% on tarlatamab vs 53% on chemo, and the CRS is well-behaved (any-grade ~56%, G>=3 ~1%, ICANS-like ~12%). That toxicity has a written management algorithm now, step-up dosing plus inpatient cycle-1 monitoring plus tocilizumab, which is exactly the kind of predictability I want before treating a young patient. The catch is honest and load-bearing: the efficacy is SCLC-derived, the osteosarcoma fit is basket-only, and the pick is contingent on DLL3 IHC SP347 >=1% (>=25% preferred for stage-1 entry). RNA elevation alone does not put DLL3 protein on the membrane, so without the IHC this ranking does not hold.
primary_concerns: Efficacy is entirely cross-tumor (SCLC); no osteosarcoma response data exist, so the DeLLphi ORR/OS numbers do not transfer cleanly.
Rank contingent on DLL3 IHC SP347 >=1% confirmation; if IHC is negative the option is foreclosed outright.
CRS and ICANS-like neurotoxicity require inpatient step-up monitoring infrastructure; deliverable but not trivial at every center.

picks.intervention_label: brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) via PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 basket NCT04262466 / next-gen IMC-P115C NCT07156136
picks.rationale: This is the best-tolerated agent in the PRAME class and that is why it sits above IMA203 for me despite weaker numbers. In the ASCO 2024 melanoma cohort the CRS stayed grade 1-2 with zero G>=3 CRS reported (0/36), the AEs clustered in the first three doses, and dexamethasone pre-medication handled them, no lymphodepletion and no marrow wipeout in the bargain. I am not overselling the efficacy: ORR was 9-11% and mPFS 2.1 mo overall, better in the PRAME-positive subset (4.5 vs 2.1 mo) but still modest. Both handles have to confirm first, PRAME IHC-positive AND HLA-A*02:01-positive, and the sarcoma slot is active-not-recruiting, so this is contingent on a sarcoma cohort re-opening or a successor protocol (IMC-P115C, NW-101C) accepting osteosarcoma.
primary_concerns: Modest efficacy: ORR 9-11%, overall mPFS 2.1 mo; the durable-responder subset is small.
Requires both PRAME IHC positivity and HLA-A*02:01 typing; either negative forecloses the entire ImmTAC class.
Sarcoma cohort active-not-recruiting; enrollability depends on a re-opening or a successor program confirming osteosarcoma eligibility.

picks.intervention_label: IMA203 (PRAME-TCR-T) via ACTengine pan-solid basket NCT03686124 (sarcoma cohort named)
picks.rationale: I will not deny the efficacy signal, ORR 54% (95% CI 34-73) with mDoR not reached is the strongest response in this dossier and the sarcoma cohort is explicitly named. But my prior weights the safety tail heavily and this one is heavy: CRS ~100% with G>=3 ~11%, ICANS-like neurotoxicity ~25%, universal G>=3 cytopenias after Cy/Flu lymphodepletion, and one treatment-related death from septic shock (4% of n=28). That is a first-in-class TCR-T with an n of 28 and a death on the board, which is why it lands at rank 3 rather than rank 1 despite the best ORR. Contingent, as with brenetafusp, on PRAME IHC AND HLA-A*02:01 both positive; I would want the CD8-TIL and HLA-LOH/B2M workup read before infusion to frame durability.
primary_concerns: One treatment-related death (septic shock) in n=28, plus universal G>=3 post-lymphodepletion cytopenias, an immunosuppression window that is real in a metastatic patient.
CRS ~100% (G>=3 ~11%) and ICANS ~25% exceed the tarlatamab and brenetafusp profiles at the same target.
Small single-arm n=28 and heavy cell-therapy logistics (leukapheresis, Cy/Flu, infusion infrastructure); durability unproven, gated on PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01.

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab + radiation therapy (DLL3 x CD3 BiTE + RT) via pan-tumor DLL3-IHC basket NCT06814496
picks.rationale: The monotherapy backbone here is the same well-characterized tarlatamab I ranked first, and the pan-tumor DLL3-IHC gate could in principle admit an IHC-positive osteosarcoma. What stops me ranking it higher is the specific missing safety datum: there is no published combination AE profile for tarlatamab plus RT, tier 5, registry-only, no results tab and no abstract. Concurrent radiation layered on a CRS/ICANS-prone BiTE is exactly the kind of potentially synergistic toxicity I do not endorse until a dedicated combination trial characterizes it, which is what this phase 1 is for. I would rather the patient take the monotherapy basket (rank 1) than the uncharacterized combination unless a specific reason for the RT arm emerges; contingent on DLL3 IHC >=1% and confirmation that bone sarcoma is on the per-protocol list.
primary_concerns: No published combination safety data (tier 5, registry-only); RT-on-BiTE synergistic toxicity is uncharacterized and is the named missing datum.
The monotherapy basket (rank 1) delivers the same characterized backbone without the uncharacterized RT layer.
Contingent on DLL3 IHC >=1% and on bone sarcoma being confirmed on the enrolling list.

notes: No toxicity_vetoes are declared in preferences.json, so no veto is triggered this round; the efficacy_toxicity_weight of 0.85 and the stated high-risk/high-reward tolerance push against my prior, and I have registered that by ranking the well-characterized tarlatamab monotherapy first rather than the higher-ORR IMA203. Every pick is contingent on the same gating fact: RNA elevation is not membrane protein. DLL3 IHC SP347 (>=1%, >=25% preferred) gates the two tarlatamab options; PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 typing gates brenetafusp and IMA203. If HLA-A*02:01 returns negative the entire PRAME half of my list collapses to the DLL3 options. I did not rank the SCLC/NEC/melanoma-only cell-therapy and radioligand constructs (ML261, DJI136, NEUK203-13, LB2102, DLL3-CAR-NK, the PRAME TCR-NK rows, radioligands) because they are not enrollable for osteosarcoma and carry registry-only or no safety readout; naming the missing datum, none has a first-in-human AE profile in this histology. The one-treatment-related-death signal on IMA203 (osteo-prame-ce-2) is the single data point most responsible for holding it at rank 3.

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab via NCT06788938 (DLL3-IHC-gated basket) — contingent on DLL3 IHC ≥1%
picks.rationale: Of everything in this dossier, the tarlatamab mechanism carries the only RCT-grade evidence. DeLLphi-304 is a randomized phase 3 with a pre-specified OS primary endpoint that hit (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.47-0.77, p<0.001; median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 mo), RoB2 Low, and the phase-2 ORR readout (40%, 95% CI 29-52) points the same direction, so I'm not relying on a single trial for the class signal. What I keep flagging: all of that is SCLC. There is no published osteosarcoma efficacy or even osteosarcoma DLL3-protein data with this drug, and the case biomarker is RNA-level, not IHC-confirmed. I rank it first among the enrollable options because the mechanism is the best-validated in the set, not because benefit in osteosarcoma has been shown. The IHC ≥1% gate is doing real work here and forecloses the option if it comes back negative.
primary_concerns: Indirectness (ROBINS-I / GRADE): every efficacy row is cross-tumor SCLC; zero osteosarcoma clinical or protein data with tarlatamab
Biomarker foreclosure: DLL3 RNA does not establish membrane protein; IHC ≥1% (≥25% for stage-1 entry) is the hard gate and is unconfirmed
DeLLphi-301 is open-label single-arm phase 2 (ORR surrogate); the OS evidence rests on the separate phase-3, so class efficacy is replicated but osteosarcoma benefit is extrapolated
Cycle-1 CRS ~51-56% and ICANS-like events ~10-12% require inpatient step-up monitoring

picks.intervention_label: IMA203 (PRAME-TCR-T) via NCT03686124 — contingent on PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01
picks.rationale: This is the one pathway where a sarcoma cohort is explicitly named in the protocol, so the indication adjacency is closer than anything on the DLL3 side. The efficacy signal that gets cited is ORR 54% (95% CI 34-73), and I want to be precise about what that number is and isn't: n=28, single-arm, no comparator, ROBINS-I Moderate, one treatment-related death from septic shock, and the responders were the melanoma-heavy basket, not osteosarcoma. A wide CI on 28 patients is a signal, not a rate you can quote to a patient. Two biomarkers gate enrollment (PRAME IHC-positive AND HLA-A*02:01-positive) and both are unknown here; HLA-A*02:01 alone knocks out roughly half of patients. Ranked below tarlatamab because the underlying evidence is single-arm phase 1/2 rather than randomized, even though the tumor match is better.
primary_concerns: Small n and imprecision: ORR 54% comes from n=28 with a 95% CI of 34-73; underpowered for a reliable point estimate
Single-arm, no comparator (ROBINS-I: confounding + no control); response-rate surrogate, mDoR not yet mature
Two-biomarker foreclosure: PRAME IHC and HLA-A*02:01 both unconfirmed; osteosarcoma PRAME IHC positivity is ~56% (Iura n=82) but this patient's status is RNA-only
Lymphodepletion (Cy/Flu) toxicity, CRS ~100%, ICANS-like ~25%, one treatment-related death in the reported cohort

picks.intervention_label: brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME × CD3 ImmTAC) — pathway, enrollability unconfirmed
picks.rationale: I'm ranking this third rather than dropping it because it has real phase-1 data, but the data are modest and cross-tumor. The melanoma readout is ORR 9-11% (4 PR of 36 at active doses), which is a genuine but low-single-agent signal, and the PRAME-positive subset separation (mPFS 4.5 vs 2.1 mo) comes from an unadjusted post-hoc split on an open-label phase 1, so I discount it. The bigger problem for this case is enrollability: the osteosarcoma-accepting basket cohort (NCT04262466) is active-not-recruiting, and the NCI's dedicated sarcoma trial (NCT07686367) enrolls synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma, not osteosarcoma. Same HLA-A*02:01 + PRAME IHC gate as IMA203. A defensible pathway to keep on the list, not a near-term enrollable option.
primary_concerns: Modest effect: melanoma ORR 9-11%; the PRAME+ vs PRAME- PFS split is an unadjusted subgroup on open-label phase 1
Cross-tumor only: no osteosarcoma data; the phase-1 evidence is an ASCO 2024 abstract, not a peer-reviewed full paper, so I have not seen the full bias profile
Enrollability unconfirmed: sarcoma basket cohort active-not-recruiting; the dedicated NCI sarcoma trial excludes osteosarcoma
Same two-biomarker foreclosure (PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01), both unconfirmed

notes: I did not abstain, but I want the record clear on how thin this is. Two of the newly added on-axis rows, tarlatamab+RT (NCT06814496) and NW-101C (NCT07266298), are tier-5 registry-only with no efficacy or safety readout and no publication at all (NW-101C has zero clinical data under that name), so I decline to rank them; recommending an intervention whose only evidence is a ClinicalTrials.gov listing is not something I'll put my name to. The DLL3/PRAME CAR-T, CAR-NK, radioligand, and ADC constructs (ML261, DJI136, NEUK203-13, 212Pb-MP0712, BL-M14D1, NG2/DLL3 CAR-T, the PRAME TCR-NK rows, OPB-201, IMC-P115C, IMA402) are all cross-tumor SCLC/NEC/melanoma phase-1 with no osteosarcoma data and, in most cases, no osteosarcoma eligibility; antigen-match on an RNA signal is not a reason to rank a preclinical or first-in-human construct above a mechanism with a positive phase-3. One correctness note for the run log: existing row osteo-prame-ce-1 carries PMID 39007852, which resolves to an unrelated HER2 breast-cancer paper. That mis-link should be fixed before anyone cites it. Every pick above is downstream of biomarker confirmation that has not happened yet: DLL3 IHC for rank 1, PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 for ranks 2 and 3. Order the IHC and HLA typing first; the ranking is provisional until those return.

picks.intervention_label: regorafenib
picks.rationale: This is the one option in the dossier with a named consensus category. NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 lists regorafenib as category 1 for relapsed/refractory osteosarcoma, resting on two randomized trials in the indication (SARC024 and REGOBONE). No DLL3 or PRAME agent comes close to that footing here. For metastatic relapsed osteosarcoma the guideline landscape is thin, and category 1 is as anchored as it gets.
primary_concerns: PFS benefit without an OS signal; both trials allowed crossover
guideline evidence assumes ECOG 0-1, which this patient meets

picks.intervention_label: cabozantinib
picks.rationale: NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 carries cabozantinib as a listed option for relapsed/refractory osteosarcoma on the CABONE cohort (ORR 11.9%, 6-month non-progression ~33%). It sits a rung below regorafenib on evidence tier -- single-arm rather than randomized -- but stays inside the guideline. A reasonable second-choice if regorafenib is not tolerated or the target-workup pathway stalls.
primary_concerns: single-arm data, no randomized comparator in osteosarcoma
ESMO-EURACAN bone-sarcoma CPG (2021) does not slot cabozantinib as a standard 2L option, so the cross-society convergence that backs regorafenib is weaker here

picks.intervention_label: DLL3 IHC (SP347) + PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing before any DLL3/PRAME-directed decision
picks.rationale: Everything downstream turns on this. The DLL3 and PRAME signals in this case are RNA-only, and every DLL3-directed trial and every HLA-restricted PRAME program gates on protein-level confirmation -- DLL3 IHC for the BiTE class, PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 typing for the ImmTAC and TCR-T class. NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 makes clinical-trial enrollment a preferred pathway for relapsed osteosarcoma, and this workup is what tells you whether that pathway is actually open. Low cost, archival tissue acceptable, 1-3 week turnaround. Ranking any DLL3 or PRAME agent above this step would be putting the drug before the biomarker that qualifies it.
primary_concerns: a negative DLL3 IHC forecloses the entire BiTE class; a negative PRAME IHC or absent HLA-A*02:01 forecloses the ImmTAC/TCR-T class
not itself a therapy -- it gates the rank-4 and rank-5 options rather than treating the patient

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab via NCT06788938 (DLL3 basket) -- contingent on DLL3 IHC >=1%
picks.rationale: Guideline-consonant only as trial enrollment, not as a recommended regimen. NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 endorses clinical trials for relapsed osteosarcoma; it does not list tarlatamab, and there is no consensus category for this drug in bone sarcoma. The mechanism has the strongest cross-tumor evidence of any option on the DLL3/PRAME axis -- DeLLphi-304 showed an OS benefit in DLL3-expressing SCLC (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.47-0.77) -- but that is a different disease, and the SCLC numbers do not transfer to osteosarcoma cleanly. Enrollment depends on DLL3 IHC (>=25% for stage 1, >=1% for stage 2), which is not yet done, and on the sponsor confirming bone sarcoma is on the per-protocol list.
primary_concerns: no consensus category in osteosarcoma; endorsed only under the NCCN clinical-trial recommendation, not as a listed regimen
efficacy evidence is entirely cross-tumor (SCLC); RNA-to-membrane-protein gap unresolved until IHC returns
CRS ~50% and ICANS-like events ~10% in the SCLC data, with inpatient cycle-1 step-up monitoring required

picks.intervention_label: IMA203 PRAME-TCR-T via NCT03686124 (ACTengine) -- contingent on PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01
picks.rationale: Same guideline logic as rank 4: consonant as trial enrollment under NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025, with no consensus category for the agent in osteosarcoma. What earns it a place on the ranked list is that the ACTengine basket names a sarcoma cohort explicitly and PRAME IHC is positive in roughly 56% of osteosarcoma (Iura 2017, n=82), so the target-prevalence prior is better here than for DLL3. The phase 1/2 signal in the sarcoma-inclusive basket is the best clinical readout in the PRAME class so far (ORR 54% in a small evaluable cohort). It ranks below tarlatamab on the DLL3 axis mainly because it needs two biomarkers positive rather than one, and because TCR-T carries lymphodepletion plus a reported treatment-related death.
primary_concerns: no consensus category in osteosarcoma; trial-enrollment pathway only
double biomarker gate -- PRAME IHC positivity AND HLA-A*02:01 -- either negative forecloses it
Cy/Flu lymphodepletion and TCR-T infrastructure; one treatment-related death (septic shock) in the 28-patient basket

notes: Framing anchor: metastatic relapsed osteosarcoma has no strong guideline-endorsed targeted option. NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 leans on cytotoxic regimens and TKIs (regorafenib category 1; cabozantinib listed) and makes clinical-trial enrollment a preferred pathway. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS-ERN PaedCan bone-sarcoma CPG (Ann Oncol 2021) states there is no accepted standard 2L regimen and does not formally slot regorafenib -- so the cross-society convergence behind rank 1 is NCCN-weighted rather than fully concordant; noted honestly rather than overstated. The DLL3/PRAME immunotherapies (ranks 4-5) are guideline-consonant only as trials: none carries a consensus category in osteosarcoma, and all are gated on the unconfirmed RNA-only biomarkers that rank 3 resolves. Verify the current NCCN version and category before any decision. User confirmed high-risk/high-reward preference, which is why the two trial options stay on the ranked list rather than being held off it -- but they sit below the guideline-anchored TKIs and below the workup that qualifies them, consistent with the concensusite prior.

picks.intervention_label: Confirmatory workup: PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing + DLL3 IHC (SP347), run together up front
picks.rationale: The patient nominated DLL3 and PRAME. Both are RNA-only right now, and every on-axis therapy below gates on protein-level confirmation the RNA signal cannot stand in for. So the single move that serves this patient's stated intent is to run all three tests at once rather than in sequence: DLL3 IHC opens the tarlatamab options, and PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 typing together open the whole PRAME class. None of it is toxic, archival FFPE covers the IHC, one blood tube covers the typing, and turnaround is 1-3 weeks. For a patient who accepts travel and wants the trial route kept open, batching the workup is what keeps the most doors open at once. I rank it first not because it treats anything but because skipping it forecloses everything the patient actually asked about.
primary_concerns: A negative DLL3 IHC or a negative HLA-A*02:01 type collapses one or both antigen axes, and the patient should hear that upfront
PRAME IHC positivity in osteosarcoma runs ~56% (Iura, n=82), so the PRAME axis is more likely than not to hold, but neither test is a formality
HLA-A*02:01 prevalence is ~40-50%, so roughly half of patients are ineligible for the entire ImmTAC/TCR-T class regardless of PRAME status

picks.intervention_label: IMA203 (PRAME TCR-T) via NCT03686124 — ACTengine pan-solid basket, sarcoma cohort named
picks.rationale: This is the pick that lands squarely on the patient's PRAME axis with real numbers behind it. The ACTengine basket explicitly names a sarcoma cohort, so an osteosarcoma patient is enrollable in principle rather than by cross-tumor argument, and the phase 1/2 read is the strongest efficacy signal in the entire PRAME class: ORR 54% (95% CI 34-73), median duration of response not reached at 9 months (Wermke, Lancet Oncol 2024). At an efficacy weight of 0.85 with an explicit high-risk appetite, this is the profile the patient said they wanted. The cost is real and I am not going to soft-pedal it: uniform CRS, ~25% ICANS-like neurotoxicity, Cy/Flu lymphodepletion, and one treatment-related death in a 28-patient series. Gated on PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01, both from the rank-1 workup.
primary_concerns: Requires both PRAME IHC-positive and HLA-A*02:01-positive; the second is a coin-flip on prevalence
Lymphodepletion plus cell-therapy infrastructure means a tertiary center and inpatient capacity, though the patient accepts travel
Sarcoma-cohort activity is carried by synovial sarcoma; osteosarcoma-specific response is not yet reported

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab (DLL3 x CD3 BiTE) via NCT06788938 — DLL3-IHC-gated solid-tumor basket
picks.rationale: The patient's other nominated antigen is DLL3, and this basket takes non-SCLC tumors that clear the DLL3 IHC gate, so it is a genuine slot rather than off-label improvisation. The mechanism carries the best cross-tumor evidence on the board: a phase 3 OS benefit in SCLC (HR 0.60, 13.6 vs 8.3 months; DeLLphi-304) and a 40% ORR in phase 2. The toxicity is more forgiving than the TCR-T route, which matters even at a high efficacy weight: CRS ~50% but mostly grade 1-2, grade 3+ around 1%, ICANS-like events ~10%. The honest gap is that all of that efficacy is SCLC-derived and there is no osteosarcoma tarlatamab data, so the DLL3 IHC (ideally >=25% for stage-1 entry) is doing all the load-bearing work.
primary_concerns: Cycle-1 step-up dosing needs inpatient CRS monitoring
Stage-1 entry wants DLL3 IHC >=25%; RNA elevation gives no read on membrane density
All efficacy is cross-tumor from SCLC; osteosarcoma activity is a hypothesis until the IHC confirms surface target

picks.intervention_label: IMC-P115C (next-gen PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT07156136 — pan-tumor PRAME/HLA-A*02:01
picks.rationale: Same PRAME axis, gentler delivery than TCR-T. IMC-P115C is Immunocore's next-generation ImmTAC after brenetafusp, and the eligibility is written pan-tumor for PRAME-positive HLA-A*02:01-positive disease, so sarcoma is admissible in principle once the sponsor confirms it is on the per-protocol list. The class read from brenetafusp is meaningful for a PRAME-positive patient specifically: 6-month OS 94% in the PRAME-positive melanoma subset versus 40% PRAME-negative, and no grade 3+ CRS in that cohort. An ImmTAC is off-the-shelf and skips lymphodepletion, so it is a lower-burden way onto the PRAME axis than IMA203 if the patient wants that trade. First-in-human dose-escalation, so this is early.
primary_concerns: Phase 1 dose-escalation; no efficacy data for IMC-P115C itself yet
Sarcoma eligibility needs sponsor confirmation before it is a real slot
Same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 gate as the rank-2 pick

picks.intervention_label: tarlatamab + radiation therapy via NCT06814496 — pan-tumor DLL3-IHC basket with RT
picks.rationale: A second DLL3-IHC-gated basket that admits high-DLL3-prevalence solid tumors, with radiation layered on for an abscopal rationale on top of the tarlatamab mechanism already central here. For a metastatic patient with an extracranial site to irradiate, the added RT arm is a plausible way to push response depth. I rank it below the plain tarlatamab basket because there is zero combination efficacy or safety data yet (registry-only, no results tab), and because bone sarcoma being on the enrolling list needs confirming. Worth surfacing as a parallel DLL3 slot if the primary tarlatamab basket is full or geographically out of reach.
primary_concerns: No combination efficacy or safety published; the RT-plus-BiTE toxicity is exactly what this phase 1 is measuring

notes: This is a re-run over the current DLL3/PRAME option set, and it lands differently from my May position for two reasons the patient should know about. First, several agents on the exact nominated antigens are now basket-eligible rather than pure cross-tumor extrapolation: IMA203 names a sarcoma cohort outright, and the tarlatamab and PRAME-ImmTAC/TCR-T baskets gate on biomarker rather than histology, so an osteosarcoma patient is admissible in principle. That is a real change in what 'trial route' means for this patient. Second, I am no longer ranking cabozantinib or regorafenib. The case scope is DLL3 and PRAME, the patient's efficacy weight is high (0.85), and those TKIs are neither on the nominated axis nor competitive on upside with the antigen-directed trials for a patient who explicitly accepts high-risk high-reward and travel. No toxicity vetoes and no modality constraints were stated, so nothing here is filtered out on a preference the patient set; the CRS/ICANS and lymphodepletion burdens are surfaced in each pick but they do not violate a stated veto. The one preference genuinely in tension is efficacy-first versus the confirmatory delay: the rank-1 workup costs 1-3 weeks before any of the antigen-directed options can start. I judge that delay clearly worth it, because without the IHC and HLA typing the entire preferred option set is unenrollable. If the patient wants zero delay, that is the tradeoff to name explicitly, and it argues for batching all three tests on day one rather than sequencing them.
